title: Holder's later bands and what became of him
summary: Holder's later bands had Budd Johnson and Eddie Durham; Tate joined the third version; Holder never recorded.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Now I wasn't in that band.
Budd was in that band. And Eddie Durham,

Eddie Tompkins, who later played with Jimmie Lunceford, Jess_e Stone[?]-- oh, had a fantastic band. I heard them, you know, but they didn't last long. He came to Kansas City and they all went but Jess Stone. So then he come back for the third time and that was the band I was in. I was in the --
He never made it really. Holder.
No, he never really made it and he was a fine trumpet player. He could play first, solo, beautiful sound, pretty and he had everything.
He's not dead. I just thought he was dead. You know, actually, I had heard he's dead, but my cousin came down from Muskogee to my Day .

He says, "Man, Holder's out there in the hospital. They've amputated his leg," say, "but he's kind of senile," says, "but he's out there." Says, "He isn't dead." I says, "Well, man, I'm going to sure write him a letter and go to see him." He'd be about 85, 87 maybe, because he and Andy are around -- you know, Andy's 85 years old.* They're around the same age.
Why do you think that was?
I don't know. Never did -- nobody just

never recorded him. Should have, because he's had the bands. And so I stayed with his band. We were in -- we were working in Seminole and there was a ballroom in Tulsa that we used to work like two months at a time and we'd go to Oklahoma City and work another place for a Mr. Steinberg, work two months and the name of that one, one in Tulsa, was Casa Loma Ballroom, beautiful ballroom, and the one in Tulsa was -- I mean in Oklahoma City was Spring Lake. That's where we were working when I caught King Oliver.
